why:
Hand ledger from the evidence alone.
RATES. Train A draws 18 L/h at all hours of all days (e4). Train B adds 22 L/h, but only between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM (e5) and only on Monday through Friday (e6). So the tank drains at 40 L/h during weekday 06:00-18:00 and at 18 L/h at every other hour, including all 48 hours of the weekend. A full weekday, measured 06:00 to 06:00, therefore removes 12 x 40 + 12 x 18 = 480 + 216 = 696 L; a full weekend day removes 24 x 18 = 432 L.
LEDGER, starting from the measured 3,100 L at 6:00 AM Monday 5 October (e3).
  Mon 06:00 -> Tue 06:00, no delivery Monday (e7): -696 -> 2,404 L.
  Tue 06:00 -> Tue 08:00, 2 h at 40 L/h: -80 -> 2,324 L immediately before the delivery.
  Tue 6 Oct 08:00 delivery of 1,800 L (e7, e8): 2,324 + 1,800 = 4,124 L, which exceeds the 4,000 L usable capacity (e2). The driver fills only to capacity and returns the surplus 124 L to the depot (e9). Tank = 4,000 L. THE CEILING BINDS HERE, and 124 L are permanently lost.
  Tue 08:00 -> 18:00, 10 h at 40 L/h: -400 -> 3,600 L.
  Tue 18:00 -> Wed 06:00, 12 h at 18 L/h: -216 -> 3,384 L.
  Wed 06:00 -> Thu 06:00, full weekday, no delivery: -696 -> 2,688 L.
  Thu 06:00 -> Fri 06:00, full weekday, no delivery: -696 -> 1,992 L.
  Fri 06:00 -> Fri 08:00, 2 h at 40 L/h: -80 -> 1,912 L immediately before the delivery.
  Fri 9 Oct 08:00 delivery of 1,800 L: 1,912 + 1,800 = 3,712 L, below capacity, so the whole load fits and nothing is lost.
  Fri 08:00 -> 18:00, 10 h at 40 L/h: -400 -> 3,312 L.
  Fri 18:00 -> Sat 06:00, 12 h at 18 L/h: -216 -> 3,096 L.
  Sat 06:00 -> Sun 06:00, train B shut down all weekend (e6), 24 h at 18 L/h: -432 -> 2,664 L.
  Sun 06:00 -> Mon 12 Oct 06:00, same: -432 -> 2,232 L.
ANSWER: 2,232 litres at the deadline. The tank never approaches empty -- its minimum over the week is 1,912 L, just before Friday's delivery -- so no dosing interruption confounds the count, and nobody at the plant can change any of the inputs (e11).
NAIVE WRONG ANSWERS. (a) The main trap: adding both 1,800 L deliveries in full and ignoring the 4,000 L capacity ceiling gives 2,356 L. That is 124 L too high, because Tuesday's load physically could not all fit and the surplus went back to the depot rather than into the tank (e2, e9). A system that models deliveries as pure additions to a stock will produce exactly 2,356. (b) A second trap: leaving train B running through Saturday and Sunday, instead of shutting it down (e6), gives 1,704 L.
